title: interactive-editing-latency-cost-benchmark-proto
content:
Purpose:
This is a working proto for an interactive-editing workload benchmark. The goal is to produce a compact, reproducible comparison of latency and cost tradeoffs for interactive editing flows (small incremental edits, rapid short-turn exchanges) versus standard chat/generation baselines. Draft, rough notes and ASCII charts below — intended to feed the product brief and a small internal spec.

Background / motivation:
- Interactive editing (IDE-like, document-authoring assist) has different request shape: many short requests (< 50 new tokens), high frequency per session, tight p50 requirements for feel (sub-100ms desirable in some cases).
- Existing chat benchmarks (single-turn long generation) understate the cost of high-turn-rate workloads and different batching/kvcache behavior.
- We need guidance for: quant profiles, batching windows, cache priming, and recommended routing (fastpath vs amortized).

Test matrix (proto):
- Models: redwood-small (quantized q4_0), redwood-base, open-xlarge (float16).
- Backends: hosted-fastpath (low-latency routed), hosted-batched (opportunistic batching window 20ms), dedicated-tiling (tiling slots), private-prefetch (kvcache warm).
- Workload shapes:
  * Micro-edit: 1-10 tokens appended (mean 6), inter-arrival per session: 200ms, session length 40 edits
  * Macro-edit: 10-60 tokens appended (mean 28), inter-arrival 800ms, session length 8 edits
  * Mixed: 50% micro / 50% macro, realistic distribution from product telemetry (sampled).
- Metrics captured: p50, p90, p99 latency (end-to-end), server decode time, queue time, batch size distribution, tokens-per-second throughput, cost-per-1k-requests (approx).

Methodology notes:
- Synthetic client harness built from chat-traffic generator (repo: PR#5826) configured to preserve jitter, client RTT distributions sampled from europe/us region traces.
- Each experiment ran 30 minutes steady-state, 10k sessions, warmup 5 minutes. Warm vs cold kvcache runs included.
- Cost approximations use reserved GPU amortization numbers from cost model v2 (linked), plus per-request infra overhead. These are approximate but consistent across runs.

Observed summary (high level):
- Micro-edit workload is dominated by per-request overhead (scheduling, RPC, handshake). For small-token edits, batching aggressively increases throughput and lowers per-request cost but raises p50/p90 by variable amounts depending on window.
- For felt interactivity, target p50 ~ 60-120ms; anything above ~200ms perceived as sluggish in user tests.
- Kvcache warm yields large decode time reductions on models with long contexts, but micro-edit benefit is smaller if edits are to the tail (less prefix reuse).

ASCII result snapshots (selected):

1) Micro-edit: p50/p90/p99 and cost per 1k requests (hosted-fastpath vs hosted-batched)

| backend         | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | avg batch | cost / 1k reqs ($) |
|-----------------|----------|----------|----------|-----------|--------------------|
| hosted-fastpath |  72      |  145     |  310     | 1.1       | 12.6               |
| hosted-batched  |  115     |  210     |  520     | 5.4       | 4.8                |
| dedicated-tiling|  96      |  180     |  400     | 3.2       | 6.0                |
| private-prefetch|  82      |  160     |  360     | 2.0       | 5.5                |
Observations:
- Hosted-batched reduces cost by ~62% vs fastpath on micro-edit, but p90 increases ~45–65ms which might be borderline for some customers.
- Dedicated-tiling sits between: lower cost than fastpath, better p50 than batch, but p99 still elevated.

2) Macro-edit: longer outputs where decode dominates

| backend         | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | avg batch | tokens per req | cost / 1k reqs ($) |
|-----------------|----------|----------|-----------|----------------|--------------------|
| hosted-fastpath |  230     |  480     | 1.2       | 34             | 28.4               |
| hosted-batched  |  280     |  520     | 6.1       | 34             | 10.6               |
| dedicated-tiling|  250     |  510     | 3.4       | 34             | 12.8               |
| private-prefetch|  210     |  390     | 2.1       | 34             | 11.9               |
Observations:
- Macro edit cost is more dominated by tokens generated — batching helps significantly for cost, and p50 impact is less noticeable compared to micro-edit.
- Private-prefetch benefits more when prefix/context reuse is present (kvcache warm).

3) Mixed workload: price-performance frontier (normalized where hosted-fastpath cost=1.0)

| backend         | normalized cost | p50 delta vs fastpath |
|-----------------|-----------------|------------------------|
| hosted-fastpath | 1.00            | 0ms                   |
| hosted-batched  | 0.49            | +43ms                 |
| dedicated-tiling| 0.54            | +24ms                 |
| private-prefetch| 0.58            | +10ms                 |
Qualitative notes and developer impact:
- UX tradeoff: for editor-mode where users expect near-instantness on each keystroke, hosted-fastpath or private-prefetch with low windows recommended. For bulk-edit or batch-save flows, batched routing yields significant cost savings.
- Product-level knobs valuable to expose: prefer-fastpath threshold (session-level), batch-window-ms override, kvcache affinity toggle, per-route quant profile suggestion.
- SDK suggestions: default editing route should use low-latency fastpath for first N edits, then switch to batched if session edit rate drops. Provide client SDK hook for affinity hints.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run with client-side prefetch (speculative next-token priming) to see micro-edit p50 reductions.
- Add real user-interaction trace ingestion (we used sampled telemetry but not full fidelity).
- Evaluate model-swap fallbacks (q4 -> q8) for rare long-turns inside editing sessions.
- Confirm cost model against finance for private deployments (we used provisional numbers v2).

Suggested outcomes for next doc iteration:
- Produce a short one-pager for platform sales with 2 simple recommended routing policies and their expected cost deltas (fastpath-first, batch-first).
- Add a small lab-run script that toggles batch window from 5ms->100ms in 5ms increments and records p50/p90/cost; attach final CSV to confluence.

Appendix: quick micro-batch window sensitivity sketch (proto numbers)

Batch window (ms) -> p50(ms) / cost delta (%) vs window=0
5  -> 85 / -12%
10 -> 98 / -28%
20 -> 115 / -47%
40 -> 142 / -59%
80 -> 210 / -70%

(Interpretation: small windows (10–20ms) give meaningful cost savings and small p50 regresses; above ~40ms, perceived interactivity degrades for micro-edit.)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally concise and a bit rough — want feedback on: additional workloads to include, other backends we should test, whether the batch-window sweep is a high priority lab task, and whether the UX thresholds (60/120/200ms) align with research.
- If approved, I'll convert into a polished internal brief + attach CSV/plot artifacts and a short slide for the next PM sync.

Author: Priya Natarajan (product/optimize)
